title: Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017
short_title: Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would exempt certain Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority documents from freedom of information requirements as part of establishing the new parliamentary expenses oversight arrangements.
The exemption would cover requests for personal advice about parliamentary work travel expenses and other documents connected with providing that advice to parliamentarians and staff.
The substantive change would begin alongside section 3 of the companion authority legislation, on proclamation or after its 12-month fallback period following Royal Assent.
changes: The authority would be listed in the Freedom of Information Act’s exemption schedule.
Documents requesting personal travel expenditure advice would fall within the exemption.
The exemption would also extend to documents about performing those personal advice functions.
summary.affected: The Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority, members of parliament and their staff are affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the bills to establish the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (IPEA) will improve transparency and public trust, while noting that 87% of current MPs—those elected after 2004—no longer receive a pension or generous travel allowances. He welcomed the authority for clarifying expense rules and providing a reference point for MPs, though he cautioned that oversight costs may exceed savings.

speeches.speaker: Darren Chester
speeches.brief: The Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017 is the first step in the biggest reforms to managing parliamentarians' expenses in more than a generation, establishing a new authority to provide clear guidance and ensure accountability. The government will continue implementing recommendations from an independent entitlements review, and a consequential amendment to the Freedom of Information Act will allow the authority to give confidential advice on travel expenses.
